# Native template map contract

`tools/generate_map_export_fixtures.py` imports the actual `exporting.py`,
`renderer.py` and `models.py`, without starting the app or reading settings.
Pillow 11.3.0/numpy 2.2.6 produce all expected pixels. The checked-in Hack font
has its complete license alongside it; production uses Windows Segoe UI/Arial.

- 54 crops/resizes cover up/downsampling, one-pixel axes, unchanged dimensions,
  alpha extremes and hidden RGB. Every RGBA byte is exact, without tolerance.
- Eight complete source TIFF paint operations cover view clipping, no overlap,
  reversed pixel scale, affine rotation, RD origins and white masking.
- Twelve page layouts capture every original drawing operation, including the
  coordinate frame/grid, scale bar, reference/legend, north arrow and attribution.
  Explicit original font measurements isolate geometry from font rasterization;
  every number and operation order is exact. Geometry is not generated by Rust.
- Ten shaping cases compare glyph IDs, positions and advances with independent
  HarfBuzz C via uharfbuzz 0.51.0: Latin/combining marks, Arabic, Hebrew and Indic.
  These assert the font's actual glyph coverage, including missing-glyph behavior;
  they do not assert that Hack covers every script or that font fallback exists.
- 32 original FreeType font bounds are retained next to native measurements.
  Native ab_glyph outlines are unhinted; HarfBuzz shaping and bidi/script runs
  replace Pillow's Windows basic layout. Glyph hinting/contours and primitive
  line joins/ellipse edge pixels are **not** claimed identical to Pillow.
  The original and native 300-DPI pages were visually reviewed.

`export_map_pages` writes a fresh audit directory. The Python verifier independently
checks every raster byte and page-plan field. With a native app binary it also
runs the real template CLI with relative TIFF/font paths, a full native map and
profile, date/project fields, permanent PNGs, DXF readback/audit and no-clobber.
An unannotated TIFF map interior is compared pixel-for-pixel against the original.

Resource bounds: 50 million page pixels, 10,000 pixels per map side, 8 MiB cached
resampled rows, 8 million coefficients per axis, 2 million CAD points/200,000 paths,
shared visible-line work budget, a 100,000-glyph shared-layout cache and cooperative cancellation. These are component
limits, not a total process-memory cap. TIFF and page buffers also use memory.
WMS reads enforce their byte limit while streaming and validate PNG/JPEG dimensions
before decoding. Export tiles share exact pixel boundaries and a pooled client;
offline tests verify all pixels across six tiles, errors and cancellation.

Map preparation is connected to template CLI/publication. Full native dialog,
photo/virtual assets, background-provider/cache parity, exact CAD text rendering
and real-project acceptance remain open in the global PARITY checklist.

Local verification: 297 Rust tests, release audit with 66,667 exact RGBA pixels
and 53,095 additional CLI map-interior pixels; two byte-identical regenerations
with different hash seeds. No whole-application performance claim is made.

The 64×64 `pdok-getmap-jpeg.jpg` is an actual public PDOK WMS response
(20 October 2026, EPSG:28992 BBOX 168000,450000,168040,450040,
Actueel_orthoHR, FORMAT=image/png). It returned image/jpeg. Its independent
Pillow decode is `pdok-expected.png`; JPEG color channels permit at most three
byte values difference (mean at most 0.5), separately from all exact PNG/raster assertions.
Source/attribution: [PDOK luchtfoto RGB](https://www.pdok.nl/introductie/-/article/pdok-luchtfoto-rgb-open-)
and [PDOK public-use CC BY statement](https://www.pdok.nl/-/luchtfoto-2025-nu-beschikbaar-bij-pdok?redirect=%2Fnieuws).
The live probe is deliberately outside the deterministic CI tests.
A complete native 300-DPI A4 template export with live HTTPS PDOK tiles
also passed DXF readback and image-content checks after this correction.
